C: Clinical photograph of the neonate's chest showing wide-spaced nipples, explicitly captioned as a feature of Turner syndrome; wide-spaced nipples is the visible hallmark of the shield-chest phenotype in Turner syndrome, and the article title confirms the disease attribution.

A: Clinical photograph of the anterior trunk of a patient with Turner syndrome showing widely spaced nipples, a classic Turner feature and visible component of the shield chest phenotype. The right upper limb posturing reflects hemiparesis from the co-occurring moyamoya syndrome, but the panel also visibly demonstrates a Turner syndrome manifestation, so it is included with Turner syndrome attribution. Image is underexposed, so skin tone is not reliably assessable. B: Clinical photograph of the posterior neck and upper back showing a classic webbed neck (pterygium colli), a hallmark Turner syndrome manifestation explicitly stated in the caption. Low posterior hairline is additionally supported by the in-text description of Fig. 1. Color cast limits reliable skin-tone assessment.
